comment: The airdress-cli revision every server build uses: the tag AND the commit it must resolve to, so a moved tag stops the build instead of changing what ships. Read by server-build.yml (release and the reproducibility check alike). v0.1.0 is the first tag of airdress-cli's collapsed history (2026-10-07); every earlier tag is gone from that repository, so an older pin cannot be fetched. On 2026-10-08 that history was rewritten to conventional commits with identical trees, so v0.1.0 now names f5eed7e; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-09 the pin moved to v0.1.3: static musl Linux builds, and credentials kept by the real Secret Service rather than the keyring library's in-memory mock store that every earlier musl build used. On 2026-10-09 airdress-cli was made public as a fresh repository, its history re-created as signed bot commits with identical trees, so v0.1.3 now names d0cdbf0; the source it builds is byte for byte the same. On 2026-10-10 the pin moved to v0.1.6 (316258753c66): the chat tools say an airdress's agent devices are off instead of advising a device join it would refuse, and the server carries airdress-cli's changes since v0.1.3. On 2026-10-14 the pin moved to v0.1.7 (e9bd69694d69): login opens the browser and waits for the approval, with the device flow kept for another device; rustls 0.23.46, and serde_norway for serde_yaml. On 2026-10-22 the pin moved to v0.1.10 (4769ab106fda): sessions are named, `@name` in chat reaches only that session, the bus addresses sessions by name, and the server takes --configured-session-name for the plugin's session_name setting. The same day it moved again to v0.1.11 (da52f5c4856d): a changed root or device key is reported as its own verdict (root_changed or device_key_changed, with signature_valid) instead of 'invalid', and `airdress agent bus repin` moves the pin after a person checks the new fingerprint. On 2026-10-23 it moved to v0.1.12 (eacc5c46886f): where the operator keeps session names (its /info lists session_names) the server registers, renames and posts by them, so a restarted session gets its name back and a clash is settled by the operator; the device host keeps the names of the sessions waiting on it; and an @-mention matching no session is answered with who is here and the near name. The same day it moved again to v0.1.13 (83923c72167e): a restarted session gets its pinned name back from the device host instead of a -3 suffix, a removed agent device waits for its Welcome instead of asking to rejoin, and system notices reach a session with their words. Then to v0.1.14 (4c1e8d42c3ea): a conversation with a named session is that session's alone, and what is written to it while it is not running reaches it when it starts. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.16 (d90d32d2451a): a session reaches a named session on another airdress by name@airdress (v0.1.15), the reachable_from_contacts setting opts one in, a message from another airdress reads as signed by that airdress's device and checked by this airdress's operator instead of 'invalid', and a session started before its device host joins the bus once the host is up. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.17 (918bd8dc7e7c): every message reaches every session and only the one addressed acts; each pushed message says who sent it and what it may ask (own devices and sessions request, everyone else informs unless the owner widened them); a reply in chat is signed by the session that wrote it, so a phone shows its name only when the signature holds; and a session finds a device host started from a shell without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. On 2026-10-24 it moved to v0.1.18 (caccba210d9f): a session that finds the plugin's session name held by another session on the machine takes a random name instead of a numbered one, and is told how to choose. The same day, before 0.1.12 was tagged, it moved to v0.1.19 (d511e4e6899d): a fresh machine needs fewer steps (login makes its own profile, device join takes the account's only airdress, the server starts the device host itself, and 'no device' says how to get one). On 2026-10-25 it moved to v0.1.20 (fcaba5e7d130): the server installs the airdress-agent this plugin release pins and starts the join itself (chat_device_join), starts the device host as soon as a join is approved instead of only at start-up, and waits for a sign-in instead of giving up when it starts first; also the read-only map tools. On 2026-10-28 it moved to v0.1.21 (a1db633a47ac): a message posted to a session by name verifies on receipt; before, the receiver hashed it without its to_name and read it as tampered with. On 2026-10-29 it moved to v0.1.22 (1a8784814df0): a reply in chat names the message it answers, a session reads it with the quoted text, is woken by a reply to its own message (and by an @-mention in it), and can reply to a message itself; the session's signature covers what a reply answers (a second signature form, while plain messages keep the first), and the host refuses a quote that does not match its own copy; airdress-mls 0.6.0, out of RUSTSEC-2026-0387 on the MLS path. On 2026-10-30 it moved to v0.1.23 (b6ce8d0066c1): a session's markdown reaches the app as blocks: the device host adds a formatted form (rich text, code, dividers) beside the text it signs, so the app renders a session's headings, lists, links and code instead of the raw markup, and the signature still covers the text alone. On 2026-10-30 it moved to v0.1.24 (c9334e755b3f): a session brings the plugin's own airdress-agent up to the pin when it starts, so a plugin update no longer leaves an older agent in place; a running device host keeps its binary and the next one started is the pinned one. On 2026-10-31 it moved to v0.1.25 (a01fb6ddefcc): a starting device host retires the key packages it published before and offers the ones its engine holds, so a phone no longer adds the device with a key package it cannot open and the session misses the conversation. The same day it moved to v0.1.26 (b90f9a3d0c05): airdress-mls 0.6.1, so a device sent a Welcome for a key package it does not hold asks to rejoin instead of losing the conversation.
